aging_ui_agm.text:
How hard your design cycles the batteries

Keep-the-food-cold list, typical year, new batteries: 134 full-cycle equivalents a year, with a median daily swing of 40% of capacity.

Renogy's page: 500 cycles at 50% depth (0.5C, 77°F). It gives no figure for other depths, so 500 is used at every depth; for daily swings deeper than 50% that flatters the battery. At that swing the sim allows 250 full-cycle equivalents before the battery is down to 80% of its capacity. The 80% end point is an estimate: the maker doesn't say what capacity is left at the end of the rated cycles.

Calendar loss: 4% of capacity a year on top of cycling. That is an estimate; no maker here publishes one. Heat and cold aren't counted in either loss.

After 1 year: about 85% health

Blackout in
25 of 25
recorded winters. Blackout per winter: median 1168 h, range 810 h to 1430 h.

Set battery health to 85%
After 5 years: below 60% health

Below 60%, well past the rated life this estimate is built on, so the winters weren't run. Plan on replacing the battery before this.
